| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |

| 3 | COU5675 | Assisting Public Sector Decision Makers With Policy Analysis | Coursera | This course provides intermediate-level policy analysis skills, including data analysis and policy/program evaluation. |
| 4 | EDX3263 | Public Policy Innovations | edX | This course explores how to innovate in the public policy space, addressing challenges and barriers, and leveraging transparency mechanisms and big data. |
| 5 | COU3249 | Data Analytics in the Public Sector with R Specialization | Coursera | This course provides advanced data analysis skills, including data visualization and R programming, to support policy decision-making. |
| 6 | EDX135 | Data for Effective Policy Making | edX | This course focuses on data collection, statistical reporting, and planning, essential for evidence-based policy-making. |
| 7 | COU4592 | The Art and Science of Economic Policy | Coursera | This course introduces economic policy concepts, including policymaking, governance, and global economic trends. |
| 8 | EDX3395 | South African Public Sector Structures, Functions, and Finance | edX | This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the South African public sector, including its structures, functions, and finance. |
| 9 | COU6457 | Politics and Ethics of Data Analytics in the Public Sector | Coursera | This course explores the politics and ethics of data analytics in the public sector, including case studies and practical applications. |

The learning path covers the full duration, with at least one course per period. The courses build on one another, starting with foundational knowledge and progressing to advanced skills. The path strikes a balance between theoretical concepts, practical applications, and real-world examples, and emphasizes critical thinking and problem-solving.

This learning path covers the full duration of 6 months, with at least one course per period. The path starts with foundational knowledge of data literacy, then develops programming skills in Python, introduces data science methodology, and focuses on data analysis and visualization. The final course, EDX1226, develops advanced data science skills, including machine learning and deep learning. EDX1024, the final course, focuses on data science with R, a popular language for data science.

**Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Foundational | COU4748 | The Modern World, Part One: Global History from 1760 to 1910 | Coursera | This course provides a solid foundation in world history, covering the major events, empires, and cultural developments that shaped the pre-industrial world. |
| Building on prior knowledge | COU5200 | The Modern World, Part Two: Global History since 1910 | Coursera | This course builds on the foundational knowledge gained in the first course, exploring the global history since 1910, including the industrial revolution and its aftermath. |
| Emphasis on contextualization and connections | COU4748 | The Modern World, Part One: Global History from 1760 to 1910 | Coursera | This course is revisited to emphasize the connections between the pre-industrial and industrial periods, highlighting the pivotal choices and cataclysmic struggles that shaped the modern world. |

**How the path fits together**

This learning path provides a comprehensive understanding of modern world history, from the industrial revolution to the present day. The path begins with a foundational course (COU4748) that covers the major events, empires, and cultural developments of the pre-industrial world. This is followed by a course (COU5200) that builds on this knowledge, exploring the global history since 1910, including the industrial revolution and its aftermath. By revisiting the first course (COU4748) with an emphasis on contextualization and connections, the learner gains a deeper understanding of the complex and often interconnected nature of modern world history. This learning path strikes a balance between breadth and depth, covering a broad range of topics while also delving deeper into specific areas of interest.

Prerequisites include a basic understanding of world history and a willingness to engage with complex, nuanced narratives. Students will develop skills in analyzing primary sources, identifying causal relationships, and synthesizing diverse perspectives to understand the complex interplay of economic, social, cultural, and political forces that have shaped the modern world. The course will cover key topics such as the rise of imperialism, the impact of World Wars I and II, the Cold War, decolonization, globalization, and the contemporary global order, with a target duration of 12 weeks.
